EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Tensions in the Middle East have significantly escalated with direct military confrontations between the US and Iran in the Strait of Hormuz, alongside ongoing, fragile negotiations in Qatar. Simultaneously, Israel has expanded ground operations into southern Lebanon and conducted a high-profile assassination attempt in Gaza, triggering further displacement and cross-border exchanges.

IRAN
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced it shot down a US MQ-9 drone in the Persian Gulf at dawn on May 26, 2026, for violating national airspace, also claiming it tracked and forced an F-35 fighter jet to flee. The US Central Command (CENTCOM) confirmed conducting "defensive strikes" in southern Iran against missile launch sites and boats attempting to lay naval mines, with reports indicating four IRGC members were killed in these strikes near Bandar Abbas and Lark Island. Iran's Foreign Ministry condemned these US actions as "flagrant and unjustified" ceasefire violations, vowing a decisive response.

Internet connectivity, previously cut for 87-88 days, began to be restored, with Netblocks reporting partial return to 86% or 34% of normal levels, though a judicial order initially attempted to halt the full restoration. Iran's President Pezeshkian engaged in telephone calls with leaders of Iraq, Oman, Qatar, Turkey, Tajikistan, Egypt, Kyrgyzstan, and Azerbaijan, emphasizing Islamic unity, regional cooperation, and Iran's unwavering stance in negotiations. Iran is demanding the release of $24 billion in frozen funds as part of any potential agreement with the US, with half to be released immediately upon a memorandum of understanding and the remainder within 60 days. Gholam-Reza Khani Shokrab was executed for alleged espionage for Israel. Majtaba Khamenei stated that regional nations would no longer serve as US shields and that the US would no longer have a safe haven in the region, also predicting Israel would not last another 25 years. Brent crude oil prices reached $100 per barrel.

ISRAEL
Israeli forces conducted an airstrike in Gaza's Rimal neighborhood, targeting Mohammad Odeh, the new leader of Hamas's military wing and former head of intelligence, who is suspected of orchestrating the October 7, 2025, attack. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and Defense Minister Katz expressed high confidence that the assassination attempt was successful. Ground operations expanded into southern Lebanon "beyond the yellow line" to "remove direct threats" to civilians and soldiers, with Netanyahu stating the aim is to "deepen operations and seize controlling areas" to fortify a security strip. Over 100 Hezbollah terror infrastructures and militants were attacked overnight in the Bekaa Valley and southern Lebanon. IDF engineering operations in Beit Hanoun destroyed over 11 kilometers of Hamas terror tunnels.

On the home front, multiple Hezbollah explosive drones were intercepted over northern Israel (Netua, Malkia, Arab al-Aramshe, Sassa), with some falling near the Lebanese border without casualties. The IDF introduced a new pre-alert system for rocket and missile fire from Lebanon, providing seconds to two minutes of warning. Defense Minister Katz ordered the immediate reversal of cuts to security components for northern communities and standby units. Prime Minister Netanyahu and US President Trump held a phone call. The committee for senior appointments re-approved Roman Gofman for Mossad chief, despite opposition from Chairman Gronis and criticism from the outgoing Mossad chief. The Ramatkal (Chief of Staff) decided to immediately dismiss the former Chief Military Prosecutor following criminal investigation. Police continue investigating a fatal car explosion in Or Akiva and a fatal shooting in A'ablin.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli forces targeted Mohammad Odeh, the new leader of Hamas's military wing, in an airstrike in Gaza's Rimal neighborhood; Israel assesses the assassination was successful. Palestinian sources reported strong explosions in western Gaza and additional strikes near the Cairo school in central Gaza. Reports also indicate several killed and wounded in a vehicle strike in Mawasi, Khan Younis. The IDF conducted an operation in Jenin refugee camp, neutralizing a militant who threw stones at forces. In Qalqilya, Shadi Jamea, a militant involved in a 2007 attack that killed Ido Zoldan, was arrested shortly after being released from Palestinian Authority detention. Hamas accused Israel of disregarding mediation efforts by insisting on its "orange line" policy in Gaza, stating it undermines ceasefire agreements and aims to establish military control.

LEBANON
Hezbollah launched multiple drone attacks against northern Israel, particularly Netua, Arab al-Aramshe, and Malkia, leading to several hostile aircraft intrusion alerts. The IDF intercepted a number of these explosive drones, though some fell within Israeli territory near the border. Hezbollah also released footage of a previous drone attack (May 20, 2026) using "Ababil" suicide drones on the newly established headquarters of the Israeli military's 401st Armored Brigade in Dibl, claiming it targeted Colonel Meir Biderman. Additional Hezbollah attacks targeted Merkava tanks in Rashaf and Zoater Al Sharqiya.

Israel announced deepening its military operations in Lebanon, with IDF ground forces reportedly operating "beyond the yellow line." The IDF issued evacuation warnings for at least 15 villages in the Tyre, Nabatieh, Mashghara, and Souhmour areas, urging residents to move north of the Zahrani River. Overnight, the IDF struck over 100 Hezbollah terror infrastructures and militants in the Bekaa Valley and southern Lebanon, including weapon depots, command centers, and observation posts. Press TV reported 17 civilians killed in Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon and claimed Israel targeted Lebanon's largest dam in the Beqaa region. The US reportedly advised Israel against major attacks in Beirut but approved targeted assassinations if opportunities arise.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Syrian authorities announced the discovery of over 70 missiles and bombs from former President Assad's chemical weapons program, leading to 18 arrests, including former senior military officials. In Iraq, National Security Advisor Qassem Al-Araji met with Iran's Deputy Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Ali Bagheri Kani in Moscow, reaffirming Iraq's constitutional commitment not to allow its territory to be used as a launchpad for attacks on neighboring countries. Anbar province in western Iraq announced an incoming wave of floods from Syria. Iraqi Hashd al-Shaabi forces facilitated the passage and provided services to Iranian pilgrims at the Mehran border crossing for the Day of Arafah. Violent riots occurred inside a women's rehabilitation center in Baghdad's Adhamiya district, with reports of injuries.

GULF STATES
Qatar is actively mediating ongoing US-Iran negotiations, which notably involved the visit of Iran's chief negotiator, Mohammad-Baqer Qalibaf, to Doha to discuss the release of $24 billion in frozen Iranian assets. Qatar's Prime Minister and Foreign Minister held telephone discussions with their Saudi, Jordanian, and Egyptian counterparts to support mediation efforts aimed at de-escalation and a lasting agreement. Qatar's Foreign Ministry explicitly denied reports of offering Iran $12 billion to guarantee a deal. In Oman, a tanker reported an external explosion 60 nautical miles east of Muscat, causing a bunker fuel spill, described as an attack. The Sultan of Oman signed an executive decree to increase trade and economic exchanges with Iran. CENTCOM stated it does not currently escort commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz, contradicting earlier reports by the Wall Street Journal that the US Navy had restarted guiding ships under "Project Freedom." Iran's IRGC Navy claimed 25 vessels passed through the Strait of Hormuz in the past 24 hours under its security coordination and warned against any violations. Pakistan's Defense Minister rejected joining the Abraham Accords despite US pressure. Over 1.7 million pilgrims participated in the Hajj rituals in Saudi Arabia.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Direct US-Iran Confrontation:** The IRGC downed a US MQ-9 drone over the Persian Gulf, and CENTCOM conducted "defensive strikes" against Iranian missile sites and mine-laying boats in southern Iran, reportedly killing four IRGC members.
2.  **Expanded Israeli Operations in Lebanon:** Israel announced deepening ground operations into southern Lebanon "beyond the yellow line" and issued evacuation warnings for multiple villages and the city of Nabatieh.
3.  **Hamas Leader Targeted:** Israel conducted an airstrike in Gaza targeting Mohammad Odeh, the new leader of Hamas's military wing, assessing the operation as successful.
4.  **Internet Restoration in Iran:** After 87-88 days of widespread outage, internet connectivity began to be restored in Iran, although initially met with a judicial order to halt the process before further restoration.
5.  **US-Iran Negotiations in Qatar:** Iran's chief negotiator, Mohammad-Baqer Qalibaf, returned from Qatar after "good" talks focused on the release of $24 billion in frozen Iranian funds, with Iran demanding half immediately upon agreement.
6.  **US NATO Troop Reductions:** The US informed European NATO allies of a planned "extensive cut" in its military deployment in Europe, including fighter jets, bombers, warships, and drones, increasing pressure on European allies to fill the gaps.
7.  **Camp David Meeting:** US President Trump is set to hold a rare cabinet meeting at Camp David tomorrow, with discussions expected to primarily focus on the escalating tensions with Iran.
8.  **Execution for Espionage:** Iran executed Gholam-Reza Khani Shokrab, accused of espionage and collaboration with Israel.
9.  **Hezbollah Drone Attacks:** Hezbollah launched multiple explosive drones at northern Israel, with some intercepted and others falling near the border, prompting "hostile aircraft intrusion" alerts.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are critically high due to direct military clashes between the US and Iran in the Persian Gulf, coupled with Israel's expanded ground operations and targeted assassinations in Lebanon and Gaza. The Strait of Hormuz remains a flashpoint with both US and Iranian military activity. The ongoing, sensitive negotiations between the US and Iran over frozen funds could easily break down, potentially leading to further military action. Active flashpoints include the northern Israeli border, southern Lebanon, the Gaza Strip, and the Strait of Hormuz. Military postures are shifting, with the US signaling a reduction in forces in Europe, while Israel is expanding its offensive capabilities in Lebanon. Red lines are being tested, including US warnings to Israel against targeting Beirut, and Iran's swift response to perceived airspace violations.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**United States:** CENTCOM confirmed "defensive strikes" against Iranian missile sites and mine-laying boats, emphasizing self-restraint during the ongoing ceasefire. The Pentagon notified European NATO allies of significant troop and equipment reductions in Europe, including fighter jets and warships. President Trump spoke with Netanyahu and is scheduled to hold a rare cabinet meeting at Camp David to discuss Iran tensions; Trump also stated Iran's enriched uranium should be destroyed in the US or in place. Secretary of State Marco Rubio affirmed that US-Iran talks in Qatar are progressing and insisted the Strait of Hormuz "must be open." CENTCOM contradicted earlier reports, stating the US Navy is not currently escorting commercial ships in Hormuz.
**Gulf States:** Qatar is actively mediating US-Iran negotiations, with its Prime Minister and Foreign Minister engaging Saudi Arabia, Jordan, and Egypt to support diplomatic efforts. Qatar denied reports it offered Iran $12 billion as a guarantee. Oman's Sultan signed an executive decree to increase trade and economic exchanges with Iran.
**European Union:** EU states, including Germany and the Netherlands, summoned Russian ambassadors following intensified attacks in Ukraine. Italy's PM Meloni stressed the importance of self-defense spending.
**Russia:** Russia's UN Ambassador was denied a US visa to attend a Security Council discussion. Foreign Minister Lavrov discussed Iran, Ukraine, and bilateral relations with US Secretary of State Rubio.
**China:** Foreign Minister Wang Yi expressed hope that all parties seize the opportunity for a resolution through dialogue and emphasized the need for any end-of-war agreement to be presented to the UN Security Council for international legitimacy. China also proposed a 5-point plan with Pakistan for peace in the Gulf.
**Turkey:** President Erdogan spoke with Iran's President Pezeshkian, pledging full support for the US-Iran negotiations and diplomatic efforts to end conflicts and strengthen regional integration.
**Pakistan:** Pakistan is actively mediating between Washington and Tehran, with its Foreign Minister proposing a five-point plan for Gulf stability in coordination with China. Pakistan also rejected joining the Abraham Accords despite US pressure.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several contradictions and unverified claims exist within the raw intelligence. Reports on the restoration of internet in Iran vary, with Netblocks reporting 34% or 86% connectivity and initial judicial orders attempting to stop it, followed by a presidential aide claiming "first step" of free access. Contradictory information emerged regarding US Navy escorts in the Strait of Hormuz; the Wall Street Journal claimed a restart of "Project Freedom," while CENTCOM and Al Arabiya denied current escort operations. Reports from Omiddana of US strikes in multiple Iranian cities (Andimeshk, Qom, Isfahan, Babolsar) beyond Bandar Abbas remain unverified by official sources and diverge from CENTCOM's specific statement on self-defense strikes in southern Iran. The timing of US strikes is also confused, with some sources reporting them as current events while others clarify they occurred the previous day. Qatar's Foreign Ministry explicitly refuted claims of a $12 billion offer to Iran. Propaganda indicators are present in both Iranian state media (e.g., strong anti-US/Israel rhetoric, Majtaba Khamenei's recycled predictions) and other channels (Omiddana's highly biased commentary, e.g., attributing non-response to "cowardice"). Reporting gaps include the precise details and full impact of the US-Iran negotiations, the exact damage and comprehensive casualty figures from the US strikes in Iran, and specific, independent assessments of the humanitarian situation and civilian impact of intensified IDF operations in Lebanon.
